_about: Operational metrics from the production multi-agent debate system over its first ~2 months in production (2026-04-08 onward). Numbers are read directly from the production SQLite ledger and audit logs; this JSON is regenerated by scripts/dump_operational_metrics.py.

stages.name: Critic
stages.structure: batches of 8, parallel, verdicts in {approve, revise, reject}

stages.name: Revisor
stages.structure: single batched LLM call across every revise verdict

stages.name: Backfill
stages.structure: 2 extra slots (diverse, defensive) when approved < target_approved

stages.name: Ranker
stages.structure: single LLM call selecting top-k for diversity / relevance / simplicity when approved > max_approved

library_composition._note: An LLM-proposed candidate factor typically seeds multiple downstream factor specs once it is composed by the downstream factor builder. The proposal ledger attributes 800 promoted factors back to the 448 materialised LLM proposals.

downstream_portfolio_attribution._status: Partial — exact LLM-input attribution to the live portfolio is being instrumented. Top-line portfolio numbers below are from the current canonical snapshot.

caveats: Numbers reflect the system's first ~2 months in production (started 2026-04-08).

The 9,592 'rounds' in the continuous-debate cron include many rounds that failed due to deployment issues unrelated to the agent logic (module path, dependency drift); the 1,214 ledger entries are the proposals that the system actually produced.
Materialization rate (36.9%) is the agent-architecture-attributable selectivity: it measures how often a raw LLM proposal survives Critic review, Revisor revision, and the auto-validation gate.
The 800 promoted factors are the output of the production pipeline that processes LLM proposals downstream; they are not single-LLM-call outputs.
